challenge.better_approach: Looked: (a) verdict every Windows clause on Linux, which is the 3a38e2e1cfe0 precedent, rejected as the only answer because it leaves a Windows green measured by the builder alone and costs a Linux hand per clause; (b) wait for 56b61c10bdbe, the Windows instance seal, which would close this as a side effect but is at TICKETME with no build. The smallest honest move is to cast this and state the dependency, so the hand is named instead of assumed.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the refusal is only the missing seal. 35bb and 1eee both refuse at the first re-run with the same line, so the measurement does not show whether the proofs themselves would pass; a seal-free run could still red.
challenge.prior_art: In-house: 56b61c10bdbe (the Windows seal, builds the seal this needs), 3a38e2e1cfe0 (Windows clause verdicted on Linux, berth verdict-20261113T024209, PROVED 11-13), 7cae18f7f9c2 and 1e99a571dd6d (the same far-box shape at other gates). Grepped tickets and questions for 'instance seal' with 'windows': no ticket names the verdict re-run as the subject.
challenge.real_collision: Possible with 56b61c10bdbe: if the Windows seal ships, this is satisfied with no change to the verdict gate. Not exclusive: this ticket's proof is the gate-side tooth, and it can wait on that build; recorded as a dependency, and the question below asks which.

answers.falsifier: On Windows, `sail.py verdict` for a ticket whose proof is green returns a verdict artifact from the gate's own re-run rather than 'exited 2 ... the instance seal is not confirmed'; a ticket whose proof is red returns fail.
answers.from_idea: none, because it is a measured gap: akiendell 2026-11-19, sail.py verdict 35bb99574043 and 1eeeab70c59e; see cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict/verdict.py and ticket 56b61c10bdbe
answers.how: First-cut, a hypothesis: the verdict gate's re-run of `bin/cairn test <proof>` is refused on Windows because the tester cannot build an instance seal without bwrap; give the Windows hand a re-run that the tester accepts (the Windows seal of 56b61c10bdbe, or a seal-free diagnostic run labelled as such), with a red-first proof that a passing proof verdicts pass on Windows and a failing one verdicts fail. No exemption: a refusal stays a refusal.
answers.traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured: a Windows green measured only by the builder's own run is a claim) and Law 8 (prove, then trust: the verdict is the peer's proof the hand did not write); Law 7 (the refusal is loud, which it already is).
answers.what: A verdict run on Windows measures its claim by a real re-run of the instrument, so a Windows clause is judged by the gate's own run and not only by the builder's validate run.

bullets.text: Measured 2026-11-19: both Windows verdicts (35bb99574043, 1eeeab70c59e) were refused by the gate's unguided re-run with `cairn test --exec: refused — the instance seal is not confirmed (indeterminate: cannot build the instance seal: bubblewrap (bwrap) is not installed); the command was not run`, exit 2.
So a green-on-Windows clause is only ever measured by the builder's own validate run; the gate cannot confirm it from here. Instances: 3a38e2e1cfe0, 35bb99574043, 1eeeab70c59e.

title: A verdict run on Windows measures its claim by a real re-run of the instrument, so a Windows clause is judged by the gat
